question.text: Start-up XYZ has 1,00,000 equity shares at INR 10, and Angel Investors hold 30,000 preference shares issued at INR 10 with conversion ratio 1:2 at INR 20/equity. A down round at INR 10/share triggers the angels' Full Ratchet anti-dilution. Under Full Ratchet, the angels will receive a revised equity allocation of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook on anti-dilution rights (pp. 291-293), Full Ratchet resets the conversion price of the earlier preference shares to the lowest issue price in the down round. At a down-round price of INR 10, the 30,000 preference shares convert 1:1 into 30,000 equity shares (instead of 15,000 at the original 1:2 ratio that assumed an INR 20 conversion price). The angels therefore receive an additional 15,000 equity shares so that they hold 30,000 equity shares in total. The Trap: 15,000 shares is the pre-ratchet, original conversion number. 60,000 and 45,000 apply multipliers that are not part of the Full Ratchet formula in the source. Note: The source-supported calculation is: revised conversion price equals the lowest down-round price of INR 10, so 30,000 preference shares convert into 30,000 equity shares with 15,000 additional shares issued.
